 LIVE Updated 24 mins ago Nvidia earnings live: Nvidia posts Q3 beat as revenue rose 103% YOY to $115.8B, board says it will not reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO
 Daniel Howley · Technology Editor Updated Tue, November 17, 2026 at 5:00 PM CST 1 min read NVDA +3.92%

 Learn more Nvidia ( NVDA ) reported its Q3 results after the bell Tuesday, beating Wall Street's expectations on the top and bottom lines and offering a better-than-anticipated Q4 outlook. The company also announced a $150 billion stock buyback. Nvidia stock rose on the news. 
 For the fourth quarter, Nvidia expects revenue between $127.4 billion and $132.6 billion. Analysts were anticipating $125.25 billion 
 For the quarter, Nvidia saw earnings per share of $2.68 on revenue of $115.8 billion. Wall Street analysts were projecting EPS of $2.47 and revenue of $109.15 billion, based on Bloomberg consensus estimates. 
 ( NVDA )
 Go deeper with AlphaSpace 155.46 -0.68 (-0.44%) At close: 4:00:00 PM EST 162.26 +6.80 (+4.37%) After hours: 6:03:45 PM EST The company reported EPS of $1.30 and revenue of $57 billion in Q3 last year. 
 Data Center revenue topped out at $107.6 billion versus an anticipated $101.85 billion. The company's Edge Computing segment brought in $8.2 billion versus an expected $7.49 billion. 
 This is Nvidia's first earnings report since CFO Colette Kress took over as interim CEO, following Jensen Huang's resignation last week. 
 Huang left the company after revelations regarding a series of affairs, including one with a suspected Chinese spy and another with an alleged Nvidia employee. 
 LIVE 49 updates 26 mins ago Daniel Howley Nvidia interim CEO Colette Kress on neocloud funding
 Kress says that Nvidia's funding guarantees to neoclouds only start when they have raised the capital that they need to build out their data center facilities. 
 33 mins ago Daniel Howley Nvidia chair Harvey Jones on the search for next permanent CEO
 "We're going to look into internal candidates as well as external candidates. The board appreciates that we're living in a world where the advanced silicon technologies and national security dynamics are making major changes in our marketplace. 
 Our new CEO will have to navigate those waters very carefully. So the search will be thorough and we want to install the permanent CEO as quickly as possible. But We won't expedited [that] before finding exactly the right person." 
 36 mins ago Daniel Howley Interim CEO Colette Kress on Nvidia's leadership transition
 On Nvidia's earnings call, CFO and interim CEO Colette Kress said, "The most important thing we think through right now is the Nvidia employees, she said, adding that they are instrumental to everything in this company. We have the best technologists on the planet, with a world-class, multi-year roadmap. From a business perspective, it's business as usual. " 
 48 mins ago Daniel Howley Hopper sales to China hit $2.3 billion in Q3
 Nvidia interim CEO Colette Kress said the company saw $2.4 billion in revenue from sales of its Hopper platform to China in Q3, but it is no longer shipping to the country. 
 Nvidia's Grace Hopper superchips are displayed at Gigabyte during COMPUTEX Taipei, one of the world's largest computer and technology trade shows, in Taipei, Taiwan May 30, 2023. REUTERS/Ann Wang · REUTERS / Reuters 
 50 mins ago Daniel Howley Interim CEO Kress says Nvidia will continue to support ecosystem growth
 CFO and Interim CEO Colette Kress says Nvidia will continue to provide support to neoclouds and will be "disciplined and selective." 
 52 mins ago Daniel Howley Total CPU revenue will double in fiscal 2028
 CFO and Interim CEO Colette Kress says that Nvidia's total CPU revenue will double in fiscal 2028. Coreweave, Meta, NScale, and OpenAI have adopted Vera, joining AWS, OCI, and SpaceXSI. 
 56 mins ago Daniel Howley Nvidia raises 2028 revenue outlook
 CFO and Interim CEO Colette Kress said Nvidia is raising its 2028 fiscal outlook, saying it now anticipates sales will climb 75% year-over-year compared to a prior estimate of 70%. 
 58 mins ago Daniel Howley Nvidia's revenue backlog is now $2.5 trillion
 CFO and Interim CEO Colette Kress says Nvidia's cloud industry revenue backlog is now a staggering $2.5 trillion. That's up from $2 trillion three months ago. 
 1 hr ago Daniel Howley Interim CEO Colette Kress says Nvidia's momentum is real
 "Our ambition will not change. Our passion to innovate will not change. And our commitment to customers, partners, and shareholders will not change," longtime Nvidia CFO and interim CEO Colette Kress said in her opening remarks as interim CEO. 
 Nvidia's Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress poses for a photo in an unknown location. Nvidia/Handout via REUTERS · Reuters / REUTERS 
 Today at 10:05 PM UTC Daniel Howley Harvey Jones on CFO Colette Kress as interim CEO
 We have an incredibly talented leadership team, and we have every confidence in Colette's leadership, integrity, and ability to deliver as interim CEO. 
 Today at 10:03 PM UTC Daniel Howley Nvidia board chair Harvey Jones says the company has no plans to bring Jensen Huang back
 Nvidia board chair Harvey Jones says Nvidia is an exceptionally strong company. 
 Says Jensen Huang voluntarily resigned from his positions as CEO, board member, and president, and that the board has no intention of bringing him back. 
 "On November 12th, our Board of Directors announced that after disclosure of personal behavior inconsistent with the company's code of conduct, standards, and cultural norms, Jensen Huang voluntarily resigned his positions as President, CEO, and board member. The NVIDIA Board unanimously accepted his resignation and does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO. The Board appointed Colette Kress, NVIDIA's longtime and well-respected CFO, as interim CEO. In addition, the Board announced it was initiating a search for a permanent chief executive, and we have since retained Haydrich and Struggles to lead the search. While this was an unexpected transition, the Board acted deliberately and in the best interest of the company's employees, customers, partners, and shareholders. This morning, the company announced that our Board has established a National Security and Export Control Oversight Committee that will include a select group of our independent Board directors, senior external advisors, and legal counsel," Jones said, according to a live transcript of the earnings call. 
 Jones added that the company will not respond to questions about former CEO Jensen Huang. "We will not be addressing or taking questions on today's call regarding the circumstances of Jensen's resignation and the ongoing investigation. 
 Today at 10:02 PM UTC Daniel Howley Colette Kress and Harvey Jones host earnings call
 Nvidia CFO and interim CEO Colette Kress and the company's new board chair Harvey Jones are hosting their first earnings call since Jensen Huang resigned as CEO. 
 Today at 10:00 PM UTC Daniel Howley Nvidia's Edge Computing segment sales climb, but PC sales continue to take a hit
 Nvidia reported Edge Computing revenue of $8.2 billion for the third quarter, up 42% year-over-year on Blackwell workstation sales and physical AI hardware. 
 But the memory shortage hit PC sales, something rivals Intel and AMD have also noted. 
 Today at 9:56 PM UTC Grace O'Donnell Nvidia's GTC events a 'much stronger signal to watch' than earnings: Uniphore CEO
 Umesh Sachdev, Uniphore CEO, said that Jensen Huang's departure as CEO has changed how he views Nvidia's ( NVDA ) earnings. 
 "Earnings have played out exactly as expected," Sachdev said on Deirdre Bosa Live, adding that "this is as good a quarter as any has been for Nvidia." 
 However, he added, "I personally will pay a lot more attention to the upcoming GTC conferences because, for me, the innovation engine — that is what Jensen was very intimately involved in and driving hands-on for the company." 
 Sachdev said that what Nvidia announces at GTC "is an indication of what happens 15 to 18 quarters out for the company. Is their innovation going to remain as strong as it was with Jensen? So for me, the GTC conference is a much stronger signal to watch in the absence of Jensen more than the earnings." 
 Today at 9:43 PM UTC What to make of Jensen Huang's apology letter: Deirdre Bosa
 Yahoo Finance's Deidre Bosa weighs in on Jensen Huang's first public statement since his resignation. 
 Today at 9:41 PM UTC Grace O'Donnell Microsoft AI CEO Mustafa Suleyman: Jensen Huang is a 'legend' but we need to know what happened
 Microsoft AI CEO Mustafa Suleyman weighed in on what Jensen Huang's departure means for Nvidia and the industry as a whole. 
 "Look, I mean, Jensen is a legend and an icon," Suleyman said on Deirdre Bosa Live . "He was certainly someone I looked up to for many years and known for a long time. I've always respected his technical achievements, and I think until we know exactly what's happened, beyond, you know, the sort of personal stuff, then you know I think it's really hard to add any further comment because some of the accusations are super serious, but at the same time we just need to know what's really happened." 
 "Nvidia is a titan, and there's plenty of chips to go around. So I'm not too worried," Suleyman added. 
 Today at 9:35 PM UTC Daniel Howley Nvidia data center revenue growth surpasses 100%
 Nvidia's data center segment revenue grew 110% in Q3, the company reported Thursday. 
 Sales topped $107.6 billion, with Hyperscaler revenue at $60.1 billion and AI Clouds, Industrial, & Enterprise at $47.5 billion. 
 Today at 9:32 PM UTC Daniel Howley Nvidia interim CEO Colette Kress says roadmap remains intact
 Nvidia interim CEO and CFO Colette Kress says the company's roadmap remains intact and that sales of its Vera Rubin platform are off to a strong start. 
 "Our momentum is real. Nvidia is an exceptional technology leader, powered by the relentless innovation of our people," she said in a statement. 
 Today at 9:16 PM UTC Grace O'Donnell SEC is investigating Nvidia, Wall Street Journal reports
 As Nvidia prepares to report earnings, the Wall Street Journal is reporting that the Securities and Exchange Commission is investigating the company, according to people familiar with the matter. 
 The full purpose of the investigation wasn't known, but it does involve the company's disclosures and whether they misled investors, the report said. 
 The investigation marks the latest headache for the AI chipmaker in the wake of founder Jensen Huang's affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese agent, and his resignation from the company, which has created significant uncertainty for the company. 
 The Justice Department is now leading investigations into Huang's relationship with Megaspeed executive Alice Huang. Shareholders have also filed a class-action lawsuit, alleging Jensen Huang misled investors about his affair with Alice Huang. 
 Before Jensen Huang admitted to having an affair, Nvidia denied that there was anything "unusual or unexpected" about his relationship with Alice Huang. 
 Today at 8:46 PM UTC Ines Ferré Huang's plea to return to Nvidia 'moves the fight from a petition to the board'
 Jensen Huang's statement that he would be "honored" to return as CEO of the AI chip giant he co-founded, if the board determines it is in shareholders' best interests, sets the stage for a growing battle over the company's future. 
 In recent days, SpaceX ( SPCX ) and Tesla ( TSLA ) CEO Elon Musk has publicly backed Huang, saying he signed a petition calling for his reinstatement. President Trump has also voiced support for Huang's return, while Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has argued that an outsider should take the job. 
 "Clearly Jensen wants to come back as CEO, and the statement moves the fight from a petition to the board," Yorkville's Dan Ives said Tuesday. 
 "The board will get more pressure from here, and activism could play a role," he added. 
 Ives noted that Nvidia's bylaws allow shareholders who have held at least 15% of the company's stock continuously for at least one year to call a special meeting. Given Nvidia's roughly $4 trillion market value, that would likely require a coalition of its largest index and long-only investors. 
 "Every director stands for election annually on a majority vote, so a special meeting would not just be a referendum on Jensen; in our view, if the board that removed him does not engage with its shareholder base, the board itself could be the one actually voted out if this plays out, " he added.
